verdict.rationale: Supermemory documents an explicit self-hosting mode where the same memory engine runs on your own hardware as a self-contained binary with local embeddings/LLM/graph engine (docs-7, docs-8, docs-16), and a public GitHub repo exists for the project (supermemory-gh-1..4), satisfying the core 'self-host on infra you control' ask. However, docs explicitly state self-hosting requires 'No Docker' and no config files (docs-31), directly contradicting the Docker-based deployment method named in the story, and there's no independent/hands-on confirmation of a successful self-hosted deployment. Missing for 10: a documented Docker/container deployment path, explicit open-source license/repo pointer for the self-hosted binary, and independent corroboration of self-hosting working in practice.
